A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same extreme image rescaling work, despite renaming OSIRDiff to TADM. All supplied pages, including extended ablations, discussions, limitations, and references, are readable, and the methods, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, timestep analyses, JPEG compression comparisons, and inference measurements.

after.justification: V3 reports original benchmark results and ablations, including additional patch-size experiments, diffusion-baseline comparisons, and memory measurements.

M1.justification: V2 Figure 2 marks the VAE decoder as frozen, whereas v3 Figure 1 and Section 3.3 add decoder fine-tuning through LoRA. V3 also writes the LPIPS and DISTS losses with a shared coefficient instead of separate coefficients. The central DFRM, timestep prediction, hybrid scheduler, and one-step denoising pipeline remain.

E1.justification: DF2K training and evaluation on DIV2K, Urban100, CLIC2020, and DIV8K remain. Both cover 16×/32× extreme rescaling, smaller-scale investigations, and JPEG compression comparisons. Revised comparison methods and patch configurations remain within this existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 and qualitative comparisons replace EDSR and RCAN with StableSR and S3Diff, while retaining ESRGAN, IRN, HCFlow, and VQIR. The efficiency comparison also adds StableSR and S3Diff. The small-scale VAE comparison introduces IRN and HCFlow, replacing the earlier comparison against the proposed 4× model.

E3.justification: The main training dataset, evaluation factors, and six benchmark metrics remain. V3 introduces a patch-size sweep evaluated with PSNR and DISTS, replaces parameter-count reporting with GPU memory in the efficiency comparison, and changes the small-scale VAE comparison from PSNR/LPIPS/MUSIQ/CLIPIQA to PSNR/SSIM. These revise auxiliary evaluation designs.

E4.justification: V3 adds comparison of rescaling error with forward-diffusion MSE in Figure 3 and patch-size sensitivity and timestep-map analyses in Figures 14–16. It removes v2's dataset-level timestep distribution analysis and replaces direct 4× model-versus-VAE testing with VAE-versus-IRN/HCFlow comparisons. The existing feature-space, SD-prior, DFRM, and fixed-timestep ablations remain.

E5.justification: V2 Section 5.2 and Figure 18 report means and variances of predicted timesteps across DIV2K at different rescaling factors; v3 removes this statistical summary. These statistics describe across-image variability. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for benchmark performance.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces all proposed-model scores: for example, DIV2K 16× LPIPS changes from 0.3026 to 0.2979 while DISTS changes from 0.0824 to 0.0886. Some ESRGAN 32× scores also change, and diffusion-baseline, memory, and patch-size results are added. Ablation and 4× results are revised. These are mixed results for a revised model. V3's Urban100 StableSR row exactly duplicates v2's EDSR row, leaving its attribution unresolved.

T1.justification: V3 removes v2 Section 6.1's bit-count derivation in Equations 14–17, which calculates a compression ratio of 24 and motivates a rescaling threshold of sqrt(24). No replacement formal bound or proof is supplied. The principal rescaling and denoising equations remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: decoupled latent rescaling, one-step diffusion enhancement, and adaptive timestep alignment improve extreme image rescaling. The TADM name emphasizes an existing contribution without substantively redefining these claims or their scope.

C2.justification: V3 develops the interpretation of rescaling as noise addition aligned with diffusion MSE and adds patch-size tradeoffs involving spatial adaptation, computation, and pretraining resolution. The retained VAE limitation is argued through different comparisons, with stronger VAEs replacing shallow-feature integration as the proposed remedy. Efficiency discussion shifts from parameter-count limitations to memory and comparisons with diffusion methods.

D1.justification: V3 adds tiled-inference pseudocode in Algorithm 1 and specifies latent patch size 96 and stride 64. It explicitly identifies the component ablations as 16× and removes total/trainable parameter counts. These are documentation changes; v2 does not establish different tiling values. Both retain SD 2.1-base, three-stage training, and the same placeholder code URL.

R1.justification: V2's general diffusion-acceleration subsection is removed, while diffusion super-resolution coverage expands substantially to discuss SinSR, S3Diff, InvSR, ResShift, and other methods. OSEDiff, already cited in v2, receives fuller discussion. V3 also removes the explicit unexplored-SD-rescaling statement and reduces the generic acceleration contribution positioning.

P1.justification: The paper and model are renamed, the refiner becomes the time scheduler, and the introduction and denoising motivation are rewritten. Related work is restructured, and the former standalone Discussions and Limitations sections become reordered subsections within Section 4.4. This substantially changes the narrative organization beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: V3 redraws the overview, removes the separate opening teaser, and reorganizes qualitative comparison grids with revised examples and baselines. It introduces MSE and tiled-inference displays, an algorithm block, and redesigned efficiency and VAE tables. Several existing displays are retained and renumbered, including the JPEG comparisons from v2 Figures 15–16 to v3 Figures 17–18.

improvement.justification: V3 adds relevant diffusion comparisons, clearer inference documentation, and useful patch-size evidence. However, its new Urban100 StableSR row repeats v2's EDSR values without explanation. Section 4.2.1 also incorrectly retains VQIR as second-best for DIV2K 32× DISTS and claims superiority across all perceptual metrics despite S3Diff leading DIV8K 16× MUSIQ. These unresolved issues affect central comparison evidence, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment despite the documentation gains.
